operations_plan.summary: Apply a constant 6.35 mm radius fillet to the currently sharp longitudinal edge of the diagonal blade member. The exact edge has no edge ID in the supplied model data, so it must be resolved by inspecting the long-edge curvature and comparing it with the already rounded corresponding edge.

steps.description: Activate solid 0 and inspect the diagonal tubular arm identified as section_1, particularly feature_1_1. Enumerate the longitudinal boundaries associated with broad planar faces 17, 19, and 21 and adjacent rounded longitudinal faces 16, 18, and 20. Measure local curvature and face continuity along each exposed long boundary. Identify the boundary having zero edge radius or a sharp discontinuity, and compare it with the corresponding already rounded long edge. The multiview images indicate that the most likely target is the visually sharp upper longitudinal edge of the broad diagonal blade in the +Z view. This edge reference remains unresolved until topology and curvature are inspected because the supplied data contains face IDs but no edge IDs.

Build the target edge chain from the sharp longitudinal edge identified in the preceding step. Include all collinear or smoothly connected portions belonging to the same physical blade edge on both exposed sides of the central clamp, where the original topology divides the edge at the central transition or hub boundaries. Limit the chain at the blade end faces and at the natural boundaries of the central transition. Exclude the end annular faces 13 and 22, the axial passage surfaces, the central circular interface face 15, and all edges belonging to feature_1_2 so that holes, end geometry, necking, and hub clearances are not independently rounded.

Apply a constant-radius edge fillet to the resolved longitudinal edge chain. Set the radius to R = 0.635 cm, equivalent to 6.35 mm. Use a rolling-ball or equivalent constant-radius solution with controlled propagation restricted to the selected chain. Do not propagate onto the blade end perimeter, axial openings, central reliefs, or clamp-contact geometry. Terminate the fillet at the existing blade-end and hub-interface boundaries, preserving the blade length, thickness datum, orientation, and central fit.

Regenerate solid 0 and verify that the new surface is a continuous convex 6.35 mm radius fillet along the complete intended exposed long edge. Confirm tangency between the new fillet and its two supporting blade faces, and inspect both end terminations and both hub-side terminations for sliver faces, self-intersections, or unintended propagation. The opposite longitudinal edge and all existing rounded longitudinal surfaces must remain unchanged.

Perform a final assembly-preservation check. Confirm that orthogonal arm solid 1 and central clamp/hub solid 2 are unchanged; verify that blade end passages, end-face locations, central circular interface, transition reliefs, clamp clearances, arm orientations, and relative assembly positions match the original model. Check that the new fillet does not interfere with the opposed rounded-square clamp bodies or alter the common pivot interface.
